plotEn:
In 1989, 40-year old actor Ian Charleson juggles film roles and his reputation for starring in Chariots of Fire while privately battling AIDS, which has begun to show on his body through Kaposi's sarcoma lesions. When Daniel Day-Lewis suddenly abandons a production of Hamlet at the National Theatre, director Richard Eyre reaches out to Ian about replacing him. Having long felt dissatisfied with his previous attempt at playing Hamlet, Ian sees this as his second and last chance to do his dream role justice. He accepts the part but discloses his condition to Richard, who reluctantly agrees to keep his secret.
On the advice of a friend, Charleson seeks treatment from Margaret Johnson at the Royal Free Hospital's AIDS ward. Johnson strongly advises against performing the strenuous role of Hamlet, but Charleson persuades her that he can continue treatment while performing. He divides his time between appointments at the hospital and rehearsals for Hamlet at the National, with friends Patsy Pollock and Sean Mathias coming to support and care for him at home. Ian spars with his friend Derek Jarman, who feels Ian has turned his back on the gay community by hiding his condition, while Ian argues he does not want to be defined in public by his sexuality or illness.
